tools.name: start_print_order
tools.description: Opens a print order. Use it when the customer wants a design printed on a garment. Call it before asking your own questions: our first reply asks for the design and the garment in words written for the customer. Pass what they have said about the order in context — a phrase or a paragraph is fine. R

tools.name: describe_order
tools.description: Records more about what the customer wants — an answer to ask_next, a correction, or a whole paragraph — and reports what is still needed. Call it each time the customer gives a new detail. In clients that render our app the customer sees their design on the garment when it changes, and the styles w

tools.name: pick_choice
tools.description: Lands one of the choices the last reply offered beside ask_next, by field and option, exactly as shown. Use it when the customer picks one of them; an answer in their own words goes to describe_order instead.

tools.name: choose_style
tools.description: Lands the order on one of the alternatives describe_order offered, by id, or on the style already chosen. Use it when the customer picks one of them; a pick in their own words can still go to describe_order. Pass color when they picked a picture from preview_colors or want the style in another shade

tools.name: preview_colors
tools.description: Shows the customer's design on the garment in other colors without changing the order: one picture per offered style per color named, up to four colors. Use it when the customer wants to compare colors or see one before deciding; `describe_order` with a new color changes the order, this compares wit

tools.name: submit_artwork
tools.description: Sends the design to be printed when you already hold a public https link to the original file; never ask the customer for one, they upload through the artwork_upload_url from any reply. We check whether it will print well at the requested size and answer in inches, with what to fix if anything. A de

tools.name: get_options
tools.description: Returns priced options with delivery dates once the order is fully described and the artwork has passed the print check. tools.name: choose_option
tools.description: Locks in the option the customer picked from get_options, and its price. Pass the option id exactly as returned. There is no way to pass a price. Free or rush delivery is chosen at checkout, not here.

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Returns the payment link for a fully specified order with a chosen option. Show checkout_url to the customer as a link labeled "Pay and enter shipping": they see their artwork and total, confirm their email address with a code we send them, then pay and enter their shipping address. Nothing is order

tools.name: resume_order
tools.description: Picks up an order that another tool refused as expired. Applies only after that refusal, with the same order_id, when the customer wants to continue that order rather than start over: it gives the order a fresh window and fresh links and returns where things stand, so you can carry on with the call

tools.name: save_progress
tools.description: Saves the customer's order to their account so they can pick it up from any conversation; a saved order never expires. Needs the customer to be signed in: if they are not, your client will ask them to sign in or create an account with us, then call this again. Applies when a response's notes offer s

tools.name: my_orders
tools.description: Lists the signed-in customer's orders with us, open and paid, each with its status. Needs the customer to be signed in; if they are not, your client will ask them to. Applies when the customer asks what they have with us, wants to pick up a saved order, or asks where an order is.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "print" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_artwork, get_options · Private data: describe_order, submit_artwork · Public sink: submit_artwork, create_checkout.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_artwork, get_options · Private data: describe_order, submit_artwork · Public sink: submit_artwork, create_checkout

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
